A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, algorithms, theorems, experiments, and Appendices A–D. The text, equations, and experimental figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original Kuhn poker simulations comparing Algorithm 2, minimax play, and OMD in Section 5 and Appendix D, with results in Figures 2–4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original Kuhn poker simulation results in Section 5 and Appendix D, including Figures 2–4.

M1.justification: The phased aggression scheme, importance-weighted estimators, OMD updates, phase transitions, and Appendix B.3 stochastic algorithm are retained. v2 explicitly supplies initial played distributions in Algorithms 1–2 where v1's pseudocode initialized only the underlying OMD iterates; this completes documentation without establishing a replacement method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate symmetrized Kuhn poker with the same All vs All comparisons and BluffJ, RaiseKQ, RaiseK, and RandMinMax opponent scenarios. The broader theoretical framing in v2 introduces no additional evaluated domain or task.

E2.justification: Min-Max and OMD with dilated KL remain the comparison methods for Algorithm 2 throughout the corresponding experiments in Figures 2–4. No comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Both retain 1,000-round evaluations, cumulative expected gain, the equilibrium-support restriction yielding delta = 1/3, and the same experimental learning-rate and unbalanced dilated-KL choices. No revised experimental protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains the same sensitivity comparisons for RandMinMax probabilities 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.3, and 0.5, together with the RaiseK case. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five repetitions, plot average cumulative expected gain, and report one standard deviation in Appendix D. The uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: All experimental panels in Figures 2–4 have identical image content, and their reported findings are retained. This includes OMD's initial losses against several opponents and its eventual advantage over Algorithm 2 against RandMinMax(0.5). No empirical result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: v2 broadens the formal game definitions to allow different action, information, policy, and treeplex spaces for the two players. Section 2 also corrects the cost-reduction identity to hold in expectation. The principal theorem bounds and the proof arguments in Appendices B–C, including the stochastic-case result, remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract now states the full-support comparator condition, changes O(sqrt(T)) to its logarithm-suppressing form, and describes regret against any fixed strategy. It also broadens the game application from symmetric zero-sum games to zero-sum games with value zero. These refine the conditions and scope of the retained central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly distinguishes the V* T + 1 loss bound for general game values from constant loss when V* = 0. Section 3.3 removes v1's blanket interpretation limiting gains against any fixed exploitable opponent and qualifies the stochastic lower-bound match as holding up to logarithmic factors. Existing adaptive-opponent and restricted-support limitations remain.

D1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 newly specify uniform initial played distributions, and Section 4.2 mentions linear programming as another way to check the phase condition. Conversely, Appendix D removes the MacBook Pro 2.8 GHz quad-core Intel Core i7 hardware specification. Experimental hyperparameter disclosures and the supplementary-code statement are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is retained, but Section 1.1 revises the comparison with Ganzfried and Sandholm (2015): v1 emphasizes gift strategies, whereas v2 describes opponent-model best responses funded by accumulated utility. The distinction concerning absent exploitation guarantees remains; other expanded main-text positioning was already present in v1's Appendix A.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introductory motivation, including a Rock-Paper-Scissors example, refines terminology and local explanations, incorporates some footnotes into the prose, and adds an Impact Statement and acknowledgments. The main section sequence and Appendix A–D organization are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the single-column main text and references with a conference two-column layout, changes typography and headers, and redistributes full-width algorithms and figures. Figure 4 moves within Appendix D, and the plots are resized while retaining their content. These constitute a substantial visual and layout revision.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision by aligning the abstract with the full-support and logarithmic qualifications already present in the technical results, clarifying the applicable game class, and removing an overbroad lower-bound interpretation. The gains concern accuracy and clarity rather than additional evidence: the main proofs and experimental results are retained. They outweigh the limited reproducibility loss from deleting the hardware specification.
